success_patterns: Clues with a hedge or category aside ('Whether it's a fruit or vegetable, it's the basis of...') were answered with the real referent (Tomato), not with one of the hedged category words.

Bare definition clues with no 'this' ('A short, witty saying') were answered with the single dictionary headword that dictionary or thesaurus passages define in the same words (epigram). Crossword-solver pages that list no answer were ignored.

Former-name clues ('His name, pre-Muhammad Ali') were answered with the other name, in the short form most passages repeat (Cassius Clay). The name in the clue was not repeated, and neither the full birth name nor a transient alias ('Cassius X') was used.

When a trivia archive or GitHub dump line repeated the clue verbatim, the agent copied the text after the clue's own '|' (Grandma Moses) and ignored the neighbouring clue's answer (Laura Bush). When the archive snippet was truncated, the agent confirmed the answer from the other passages.

Setting, pun and stage-direction lead-ins ('Neatness does count --', '(Jimmy of the Clue Crew ...)') were treated as decoration. The agent matched the factual core (antiseptics, premiered 1951) to one entity that recurs across passages, and gave the bare standard title or name.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already covers verbatim archive hits, head-noun trimming and decoration. Three gaps remain. First, the 'clue lists its own options' rule could be misapplied to hedge phrases like 'a fruit or vegetable', and one successful trajectory had to avoid that trap. Second, bare definition clues without 'this' have no explicit guidance. Third, former-name clues have no explicit guidance, nor does the rule that the answer follows its own clue in multi-clue dumps. These three short additions reinforce behaviors that worked.

edits.target: - Clue lists its own options ('Of North Park, East Park, West Park or South Park, it's where...'): the answer is exactly one of the listed options, copied verbatim. Use the context to pick which.
edits.content: - Do NOT apply that rule to a hedge about the category ('Whether it's a fruit or vegetable, it's the basis of pomodoro & marinara sauces', 'whether you call it X or Y'). The listed words are just a side-comment and are not the answer. Answer the concrete thing the rest of the clue describes ('Tomato'), as a plain common noun.

edits.target: - Double-meaning clues ('Term for an international match, or what its players are "put to"', 'X, or Y'): the answer is ONE word that satisfies BOTH halves ('the Test': a Test match; 'put to the test'). Check every candidate against both halves. A dictionary synonym that fits only one half ('trial') is wrong. When passages are noisy, use your own knowledge of sports terms and idioms.
edits.content:
- Bare definition clues with no 'this' ('A short, witty saying') ask for the word being defined. Find the dictionary or thesaurus line that gives the same gloss ('epigram: a witty, ingenious, or pointed saying tersely expressed') and answer with that headword alone, in singular dictionary form. Ignore crossword-solver pages that only repeat the clue. Do not answer with a longer descriptive phrase or a loose synonym such as 'quip' unless the passages gloss it in the clue's own words.
- Former-name clues ('His name, pre-Muhammad Ali', 'née', 'formerly', 'born as'): the answer is the OTHER name, never the one already in the clue. Choose the short form the passages repeat most ('Cassius Clay', not 'Cassius Marcellus Clay Jr.' and not a transient alias like 'Cassius X').

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - In multi-clue archive dumps (GitHub question files, TriviaBistro pages) several 'clue | answer. right: Name.' entries sit back to back. Locate the entry whose clue text matches the question, then take the answer after THAT clue's '|'. The answer on the line above belongs to a different clue, and the contestant name after 'right:' is not part of the answer. If the archive snippet cuts off before the answer, answer with the entity that the other passages tie to the clue's details.
